title: Charles Leclerc reveals Ferrari summons message after Lewis Hamilton collision
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc has revealed that Fred Vasseur told him what he did was "not acceptable" immediately after the Las Vegas Grand Prix, following his collision with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton.

The Ferrari boss delivered a radio message to Leclerc immediately after the race, telling the Monegasque he wanted to see him before his media duties.

The clash happened on Lap 38 at Turn 7, when Leclerc's front-right wheel made contact with Hamilton's rear-left corner, spinning the seven-time champion down the order.

The FIA stewards handed Leclerc a 10-second time penalty, ruling that he had started his move from too far back and had not earned the right to the corner. Leclerc eventually finished 10th, with Hamilton recovering to seventh.

It cost the Scuderia a potential podium, but certainly a significantly greater haul of points just a matter of weeks after the duo clashed in Mexico City.

Speaking to Viaplay after the race, Leclerc was asked what Vasseur had said to him.

"That it was not acceptable again," Leclerc revealed. "I think it's been too many times, but I took the 10-second penalty, which means that I am predominantly at fault in this clash, and I'll take the blame for that.

"I don't feel it's very different compared to the wheel-to-wheel clashes we've had in the past, and I don't think there was any overdriving there whatsoever. Just by the situation that Lewis had with the McLaren in front, there was a natural opportunity for me to be down the inside there.

"There was a lot of space. I think just by the angle of the car, Lewis probably didn't see in the mirrors that I was inside, and so there was very little space then at the apex, not to blame Lewis.

"But at the end of the day, it's not acceptable to lose a lot of points because I take a penalty; on top of that, Lewis probably had damage on his car. It's, yeah, it feels very bad."

Leclerc set for Las Vegas personal reflection

Asked what needed to change following the incident, Leclerc was reluctant to go into detail about what had passed between himself and Vasseur.

"Listen, it's a tricky situation to be here and to kind of speak of what we speak inside the team," said Leclerc. "So I do understand that you guys [the media] want to know a lot about it, but also for me, it's a tricky situation to kind of go into details of whatever we tell ourselves.

"At the end of the day, I think the result is that today, because of something I did, we don't score the points that we should have, and that is not acceptable.

"I will look back at the incident and try to understand what I could have done better, differently, and to make sure that I don't ever find myself in this situation again. That's all I can say."

title: Isack Hadjar suffers insult to injury with Las Vegas penalty
excerpt:
Isack Hadjar has been handed a 10-second time penalty added to his overall race time at the Las Vegas Grand Prix for driving unnecessarily slowly under safety car conditions.

Hadjar was running second ahead of George Russell when the safety car came out following Sergio Perez and Rafael Camara's collision in Sin City.

With Max Verstappen leading, the French driver opted to back up and create a sufficient gap for Red Bull to pull off a double-stack pit stop.

This resulted in his RB22 travelling over 100km/h slower down the straight between Turns 13 and 14 at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit than his team-mate.

The official stewards' decision document stated: "While driving on the straight between Turns 13 and 14 under Safety Car conditions, the driver of Car 6 received repeated instructions from his team stating 'five seconds, five seconds, five seconds'.

"Following these instructions, Car 6 significantly reduced its speed, at one point travelling approximately 100 km/h slower than Car 3, which was ahead of it.

"The Stewards determined that this significant reduction in speed was deliberate and intended to create a gap to the car ahead and was not made for safety reasons, thereby allowing the team to perform a double-stack pit stop without Car 6 losing time waiting behind its teammate in the pit lane.

"Furthermore, this manoeuvre directly impacted the cars following Car 6, which were forced to reduce their speed accordingly and could not overtake Car 6 due to the restrictions applicable under Safety Car conditions.

"The Stewards considered that Car 6 was driving unnecessarily slowly for tactical reasons and that such conduct constituted a breach of the applicable regulations.

"In reaching their decision, the Stewards also took into account the precedent involving Car 4 (Norris) at the 2023 Canadian Grand Prix, where a penalty was imposed for similar conduct.

"The Stewards imposed a 10 seconds time penalty, which is consistent with the 2026 F1 Penalty Guidelines."

The punishment has little bearing in the grand scheme of things, with it dropping Hadjar from P14 to P15, behind only Liam Lawson.

He was only running so low down the order due to a front wing failure following that pit stop phase, which saw the component suddenly collapse under his car, necessitating a change. Before that, the 21-year-old had been in contention for at least a podium finish.

title: F1 driver handed significant Qatar GP grid penalty after Las Vegas calamity
excerpt:
Sergio Perez has been handed a five-place grid penalty for next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix after causing a collision with Rafael Camara during the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The Cadillac driver was originally given a 10-second time penalty for the clash at Turn 14, but as Perez retired from the race, the stewards converted the sanction into a grid drop for Lusail.

Applying the driving standards guidelines, the stewards ruled that Perez had not earned the right to the corner and was wholly to blame for the collision.

For Camara, it has been a difficult introduction to F1 after he made his debut in very challenging conditions last time out in Brazil.

title: Max Verstappen unleashes unbelievable verbal attack on George Russell
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has fired off his latest round of criticism at George Russell following the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Verstappen scored his 75th career victory on Saturday night, coming out on top in a frantic race that saw 34 overtakes for the lead.

Among those who were battling for the top spot was George Russell, who spent the early stages of the race trading the lead with Verstappen.

However, in the latter stages of the race, Russell locked up and hit the barrier as he attempted to overtake teammate Kimi Antonelli for second place.

It was a devastating mistake for the Briton and another setback in a year of challenges.

Russell and Verstappen came to blows on Friday evening during final practice, with Russell declaring afterwards that "someone has to stand up" to Verstappen, reigniting the feud that kicked off two years ago.

While many expected the fireworks to continue during the race, the biggest talking point came after the chequered flag.

[Article continues below]

Verstappen states Russell 'so far below my level'

Verstappen was positioned in the press conference room when he was asked about the situation with Russell.

The four-time champion did not hold back in his criticism of him and indicated that he was pleased to see his rival find the wall during the race.

"The thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track," Verstappen told media including RacingNews365.

"For me it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that.

"So it doesn't bother me. And, today, karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening.

"I was like 'fantastic, my day is only getting better'. And when I crossed the line in first, my day was complete."

title: Lewis Hamilton calls on Ferrari to 'figure it out' after fresh Charles Leclerc drama
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton hopes Ferrari can resolve its driver dilemma after yet another incident with team-mate Charles Leclerc at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Hamilton was spun around by Leclerc as the pair fought over sixth place on Lap 38 of 50 in Sin City, for which the latter was given a 10-second time penalty.

The seven-time F1 drivers' champion put the onus on the team to fix the problems the pair have experienced with wheel-to-wheel racing of late.

At the Mexico City Grand Prix, their first-lap battle cost them a likely victory from a strong 1-2 position.

That led to harsh words from team principal Fred Vasseur, who has reiterated that stance now, and Hamilton did not hold back, either, with his comments in the weeks that followed.

However, after talks at the previous round in São Paulo, both the British driver and Leclerc were keen to put the tensions behind them and work together moving forward.

That was short-lived. But unlike last time, Hamilton was unwilling to remark on the latest incident.

"I'm not going to get into the scenario today," he told Sky Sports F1 after recovering to seventh in Nevada. "That's something for you to speak to Ferrari about."

[Article continues below]

Hamilton: team orders for Ferrari 'to decide'

Instead, Hamilton focused on his evening under the lights of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit. He highlighted the difficulties the SF-26 endured with its underpowered power unit and the 10-second time penalty he earned for leaving the track and gaining an advantage during an early-race battle with Lando Norris and Leclerc.

"But we knew that we were faced with a massive challenge this weekend," he added. "We didn't realise that there would be such a limitation on these straights, and the qualifying obviously was difficult.

"In the race, I felt great, and I really was progressing well. I really ultimately wanted to try and make sure we finish ahead of the McLarens...

"And then avoiding collision with one of the McLarens got me a 10-second penalty, which was, I think, really harsh, which was frustrating.

"But I just got my head back down and just kept chasing. Managed to get back in the fight, and then again got knocked back again.

"I never gave up, and I really was just trying to get the best results. I really think we could have had a podium today with the pace we had."

Given the apparent inability of Hamilton and Leclerc, for which most blame has been placed at the feet of the latter, to live harmoniously on track and fight for the betterment of the Scuderia, the former was asked whether team orders and rules of engagement must now be implemented.

"That's for Ferrari to decide," Hamilton replied. "Obviously, I've done all I can, and I've said everything and more... it's been difficult.

"So all I can do is just show up and give it everything I can, and hopefully in the background they eventually figure it out."

title: Charles Leclerc summoned by Ferrari boss after latest Lewis Hamilton aggression
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc was called to visit Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur before his media commitments at the Las Vegas Grand Prix after spinning Lewis Hamilton.

Leclerc hit the rear of his team-mate's car during the 50-lap race in Sin City, dropping the seven-time F1 drivers' champion down the order.

It also harmed his evening in Nevada, with Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto capitalising on the mistake and getting ahead.

Leclerc ultimately got back in front of the latter Alpine, taking the chequered flag in sixth. The 10-second time penalty he earned for the collision dropped him to P10.

Hamilton therefore finished in eighth after recovering slightly and being aided by George Russell's late-race error, which saw the Mercedes driver fall from the podium places to ninth.

However, after recent tensions at Ferrari over how Leclerc races against Hamilton, which were sparked by their clash in Mexico City, Vasseur wanted to speak to the Monegasque driver before his press duties.

Talks were held at the previous round in São Paulo to clear the air, but evidently they did not do the trick.

Both Leclerc and Hamilton had moved to quell the narrative after some choice words, particularly from the British driver, but that will be reignited now, despite the latter trying to prevent his team-mate being penalised for the indiscretion.

Speaking over team radio on the cool-down lap, Vasseur said: "Charles, I want to see you just after the race, before everything."
